title: Capacity vs tolerance: build for the lower
objectives: Distinguish risk capacity from risk tolerance.
Explain the rule to build for the lower of the two, with the four combinations.
body_md:
Capacity and tolerance often disagree. When they do, build for the lower one.

## The two ideas

- Risk capacity: the financial ability to bear losses. Stable income, no loans, a large buffer and other assets raise it.
- Risk tolerance: the emotional willingness to bear losses. A questionnaire and past behaviour in a fall reveal it.

## The four combinations

| | High tolerance | Low tolerance |
|---|---|---|
| High capacity | More equity is possible | Build for tolerance, and educate over time |
| Low capacity | Build for capacity | Most conservative mix |

## The cases to watch

- Young, well paid, but sold in the 2020 fall: high capacity, low tolerance. Build for tolerance; the client will grow into more equity.
- Keen on risk but has dependants and loans: high tolerance, low capacity. Build for capacity.
- Nervous-sounding with a 20-year horizon: may need help taking enough equity to beat inflation, slowly.

Ask about losses in rupees, not percentages: "If your ₹10 lakh became ₹7.5 lakh in a bad year, what would you do?"
example: A 29-year-old engineer with a stable job, no loans and a year of expenses saved sold everything in March 2020. His capacity is high; his tolerance is low. The mix is built for tolerance, with a plan to revisit after the next full cycle.
say: When capacity and comfort disagree, we build for the lower one.
If your ₹10 lakh became ₹7.5 lakh in a bad year, what would you do?
never: You're young, so 90% equity is fine.
Nervous clients should stay in FDs.

talk_track.title: Capacity vs tolerance: build for the lower one
talk_track.text: Capacity and tolerance often disagree, and when they do, build for the lower one. High capacity but low tolerance, like a young, well-paid client who sold in the 2020 fall: build for their tolerance, and educate them over time. High tolerance but low capacity, like a client keen on risk who has dependants and loans: build for their capacity. And neither able nor willing to take losses: that client needs the most conservative mix.

check.q: A client has high risk capacity but low risk tolerance. What do you build for?
check.why: Always build for the lower of the two.

check.q: What is the difference between capacity and tolerance?
o: Capacity is emotional; tolerance is financial
Capacity is the financial ability to bear losses; tolerance is the emotional willingness
check.why: Capacity is financial, tolerance is emotional. When they disagree, build for the lower one.

check.q: Why ask about losses in rupees rather than percentages?
o: Because a rupee figure makes the loss concrete and gets an honest answer
check.why: If your ten lakh became seven and a half lakh lands far better than minus twenty-five percent.
